profileImage.note: Set type to 'github' to use GitHub profile image, 'display' to use display.profileImage, or 'custom' to use customUrl. Colors support ANY CSS format: hex (#a855f7), rgb, rgba, hsl, named colors, or Tailwind classes (purple-500)

copyData.tooltip: Copy this portfolio as text an AI can read

home.note: Configure the home page content - greeting, name, typewriter strings, description, profile image settings, buttons, social links, and animations

about.heading: About Me

image.note: Set type to 'github' to use GitHub profile image, 'home' to use same as home page, or 'custom' to use customUrl

about.note: Configure the About page content - heading, subheading, title, paragraphs, image settings, skills section heading, and skills categories with items
about.skillsNote: Comprehensive skills showcase covering programming languages, frameworks, AI/ML tools, cloud platforms, and emerging technologies. Each skill includes relevant icons and color coding for better visual representation.
about.statsNote: Updated statistics reflecting real achievements including hackathon winnings, research publications, and technical certifications. Numbers are based on actual portfolio data and accomplishments.

socialPreview.note: opengraphVariant can be 0,1,2,etc and mostly changes cache behavior. If GitHub OpenGraph is rate-limited, card falls back to custom image and users can switch sources when both are available.

projects.staticProjectsNote: Configure static projects when mode is set to 'static'. Each project should have: id, name, description, technologies array, category, featured (boolean), showInAbout (boolean), status, startDate, endDate (null for ongoing), githubUrl, liveUrl, demoUrl, documentationUrl, imageUrl, tags array, highlights array, and stats object with stars/forks/watchers/issues
projects.featuredProjectsConfigNote: Configure visual styling for projects that appear in the About page (projects with showInAbout: true). Each project's name should match a key in featuredProjectsConfig. Use cohesive color schemes that align with your brand. Visit https://react-icons.github.io/ to find appropriate icons.

resume.note: Resume URL - can be a relative path (for local files) or a full URL (for external). If the RESUME_LINK environment variable is set, it will override this value.
resume.sectionOrderNote: Configure the order in which resume sections appear. Available sections: experiences, education, skills, personalProjects, certifications, awards, publications, languages, volunteerExperience
resume.experiencesNote: Configure work experience entries - each should have title, company, period, location, and description array
resume.educationNote: Configure education entries - each should have degree, field, school, period, gpa, and achievements array
resume.skillsNote: Configure skills with categories and items. Each item should have name, icon, and color. Available icons: same as About page skill icons.
resume.certificationsNote: Configure certifications with machine-readable validity metadata. Recommended fields: name, issuer, issueDate (YYYY-MM-DD), hasExpiry (boolean), expiryDate (YYYY-MM-DD or empty when hasExpiry is false), credentialId, certificateUrl, and verificationUrl.
resume.awardsNote: Configure awards and recognitions - each should have name, organization, date, description, and optional rewardAmount. URLs are optional: verificationUrl (to verify the award) and certificateUrl (to view certificate). Links will only show if provided.
resume.publicationsNote: Configure publications - each should have title, type, publisher, date, url (optional), and description
resume.languagesNote: Configure languages - each should have name, proficiency, and level (A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2)
resume.volunteerExperienceNote: Configure volunteer experience - each should have role, organization, period, and description array
resume.personalProjectsNote: Configure personal projects - each should have name, technologies array (with icon and color), period, description, githubUrl (optional), liveUrl (optional), demoUrl (optional), documentationUrl (optional)

social.note: Configure all social media platforms here. Set enabled: true and provide URL to activate. Use showInHome, showInFooter, showInContact to control where each platform appears. To add new platforms, add a new object with name, key, icon, url, label, color, hoverColor, and show flags. Available icons: FaGithub, FaLinkedin, FaTwitter, FaInstagram, FaDiscord, FaYoutube, FaTwitch, FaTiktok, FaMedium, FaDev, FaStackOverflow, FaDribbble, FaBehance, FaCodepen, ArrowUpIcon, Bars3Icon, XMarkIcon

contact.subtitle: Whether it's a hackathon, a startup idea, or an interesting open-source project — I'm always up for a conversation. Let's build something worth showing off.
contact.note: Configure the Contact Page layout, sections, and content. The Contact Page supports a flexible two-column layout with configurable sections. You can rearrange sections, change titles, add/remove sections, and control what content appears where. Available section types: 'contactInfo' (email, phone, location), 'currentFocus' (what you're working on), 'quickActions' (action buttons with icons), 'github' (GitHub profiles), 'social' (social media platforms), 'collaboration' (collaboration interests). Each section can be shown/hidden and have custom titles. The 'github' and 'social' sections automatically pull from the configured platforms and will display in a grid layout. Platforms with descriptions will be displayed horizontally with text, while simple platforms will show as icon-only cards. Social platforms can be filtered to show only on Contact Page by setting showInContact: true and other show flags to false.

logo.note: Set type to 'text' for text logo, 'image' for custom image, 'github' for GitHub profile image, or 'auto' to match home profileImage settings. githubUsername overrides projects.devUsername for navbar only.

navbar.note: Configure navbar logo, navigation items, styling, and animations

footer.note: Enhanced footer with configurable stats, optional quick links (disabled since navbar is always visible), dynamic project counting, and improved layout

favicon.note: Set type to 'github' to use GitHub profile image, 'custom' to use customUrl, 'icon' to use React Icons from react-icons.github.io, or 'default' for default favicon. For 'icon' type, visit https://react-icons.github.io/react-icons and use any icon name (e.g., FaReact, SiJavascript, MdHome). githubUsername overrides projects.devUsername for favicon only. For best tab clarity, prefer local PNG assets like '/favicon-32x32.png'.

projectMapping.note: Maps repository names to CounterAPI project names
